title: Cardiovascular Outcomes Trials for Diabetes and Obesity Drugs: FDA and EMA Review of MACE Endpoints and Noninferiority Margins
summary: How FDA and EMA reviewed CVOTs for diabetes and obesity drugs: accepted 3-point MACE definitions, the 1.8 and 1.3 noninferiority margins, and how results reached labeling.
body_markdown:
## Cardiovascular outcomes trials for diabetes and obesity drugs: how FDA and EMA judged MACE endpoints and noninferiority margins


FDA and EMA have both treated cardiovascular (CV) safety as a central question in diabetes and obesity drug development. They have also converged on the same core endpoint: three-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Where they differ is in how the margins were set and in how a positive CVOT result reaches the label. This article covers the guidance frameworks, the MACE definitions and noninferiority margins regulators accepted in individual programs, and how each agency turned CVOT results into labeling.


### Key takeaways


- **Standard endpoint.** Both agencies accepted time to first 3-point MACE (CV death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke) as the primary endpoint in nearly every CVOT reviewed here, with independent adjudication[370](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=370)[172](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=172)[876](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=876) .
- **FDA's 1.8 / 1.3 framework.** Under the December 2008 FDA guidance, sponsors had to exclude an upper 95% confidence bound of 1.8 for the CV risk ratio before approval. If the bound fell between 1.3 and 1.8, a postmarketing trial generally had to exclude 1.3[977](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=977)[978](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=978) . In March 2020, a draft guidance proposed replacing this approach with minimum safety-database requirements[154](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=154)[921](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=921)[922](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=922) .
- **EMA's approach is less prescriptive.** The CHMP reflection paper treats an upper bound below 1.8 (when the HR is about 1) as a reasonable planning assumption at initial licensing. It does not present 1.8 as a universal margin[879](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=879) .
- **Margins actually accepted.** These ranged from 1.8 (SUSTAIN 6, PIONEER 6), to the common 1.3 (LEADER, EMPA-REG OUTCOME, CANVAS, DECLARE, VERTIS CV, SAVOR, EXAMINE, CARMELINA, DEVOTE, EXSCEL, ELIXA, TECOS), to 2.0/1.4 for an obesity drug (LIGHT), to 1.05 for an active-comparator CVOT (SURPASS-CVOT). Some trials were designed for superiority with no margin at all (SELECT)[543](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=543)[769](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=769)[371](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=371)[706](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=706)[241](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=241)[200](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=200)[23](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=23) .
- **Labeling diverges.** FDA has granted standalone indications to reduce MACE risk (for example Victoza, Ozempic, Invokana, Wegovy)[374](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=374)[854](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=854)[422](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=422)[952](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=952) . CHMP has repeatedly declined separate CV-prevention indications in SmPC section 4.1. Instead it broadens the type 2 diabetes wording and places the CVOT results in section 5.1[341](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=341)[99](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=99)[66](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=66)[678](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=678)[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=27)[203](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=203) .


### The FDA framework


#### The 2008 guidance and how reviewers applied it


FDA's December 2008 guidance, *Diabetes Mellitus: Evaluating Cardiovascular Risk in New Antidiabetic Therapies to Treat Type 2 Diabetes* , recommended CVOTs and prospective meta-analyses for new antidiabetic therapies[152](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=152)[153](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=153) . FDA reviews describe its decision rules this way[977](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=977)[978](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=978)[979](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=979) :


- Before approval, sponsors compare CV events against a control group. They must show that the upper bound of the two-sided 95% CI for the estimated risk ratio is below 1.8, with a reassuring point estimate.
- If the upper bound falls between 1.3 and 1.8 and benefit-risk supports approval, a required postmarketing trial generally must establish an upper bound below 1.3.
- If premarketing data already exclude 1.3, a postmarketing trial generally may not be needed.
- Events should be prospectively and blindly adjudicated, ideally within a prespecified phase 2/3 meta-analysis. A large safety trial can also supply the preapproval bound, alone or combined with other trials.


In practice, sponsors used two steps. A pooled, adjudicated phase 2/3 meta-analysis excluded 1.8, and a dedicated CVOT then excluded 1.3[994](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=994) . Program examples:


- The Farxiga meta-analysis pooled 21 trials[982](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=982)[983](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=983) .
- The Invokana, Steglatro, Tanzeum and Trulicity reviews describe meta-analyses that often used adjudicated MACE+ (MACE plus hospitalization for unstable angina) to test the 1.8 margin[984](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=984)[985](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=985)[986](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=986)[987](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=987) .
- For Jardiance, the eight-trial meta-analysis included interim CVOT data. FDA said the dedicated CVOT should provide the 1.3 assessment, rather than drawing conclusions from overlapping data sources without multiplicity control[988](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=988)[989](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=989) .
- For Mounjaro, a seven-trial MACE-4 meta-analysis was used against the 1.8 margin[791](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=791) .


Not every product was held to this framework:


- Onglyza and Victoza were caught by the guidance after development or submission was already under way. Reviewers acknowledged that retrospective event analyses could not fully replace prospective adjudication[980](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=980)[981](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=981) .
- The Tresiba review states that injectable insulins were not generally held to the 1.8/1.3 bounds, although FDA still expected CV events to be collected and analyzed[993](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=993) . DEVOTE nonetheless prespecified a 1.3 margin[649](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=649) .


#### The 2020 draft guidance


In March 2020 FDA issued the draft guidance *Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Evaluating the Safety of New Drugs for Improving Glycemic Control* . It proposes withdrawing and replacing the 2008 guidance[154](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=154) . FDA gave two reasons. First, none of the CVOTs completed since 2008 had found an increased risk of ischemic CV events, and some showed reduced risk[919](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=919) . Second, a 2018 advisory committee recommended postmarketing requirements tied to program-specific risk signals rather than a one-size-fits-all approach[916](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=916) .


In place of a fixed risk margin, the draft asks for a minimum safety database[921](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=921)[922](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=922) :


Element Recommended minimum


Total phase 3 exposure 4,000 patient-years


Long-term exposure 1,500 patients for at least 1 year; 500 patients for at least 2 years


High-risk subgroups 500 with stage 3/4 CKD; 600 with established CV disease; 600 older than 65


Overlap target At least 1,200 patients with at least one of these characteristics


The draft keeps rigorous adjudication of CV events. Where a specific premarket concern exists, enough events may still be needed to exclude a meaningful degree of risk[923](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=923) .


#### Obesity drugs


The January 2025 FDA draft guidance *Obesity and Overweight: Developing Drugs and Biological Products for Weight Reduction* recommends:


- monitoring cardiometabolic parameters and running a comprehensive CV assessment, generally including ambulatory blood-pressure monitoring[748](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=748)[749](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=749)
- a CVOT if a CV risk signal emerges, either before or after approval depending on the signal[750](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=750)


The guidance passages reviewed do not set a MACE endpoint or a numerical risk margin[751](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=751) .


### The EMA framework


#### Diabetes guideline


Revision 1 of the CHMP *Guideline on clinical investigation of medicinal products in the treatment or prevention of diabetes mellitus* (29 June 2012) sets out the following:


- **MACE definition.** The principal MACE are CV death, non-fatal MI and stroke. Hospitalization for unstable angina may be added when the composite's main purpose is to exclude a safety signal[172](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=172) .
- **Adjudication and pooling.** CV outcomes should be predefined consistently, centrally adjudicated with blinding, and pooled under a prospective statistical plan[173](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=173) .
- **Two routes to the evidence.** One is a meta-analysis, provided the database can detect uncommon serious events. The other, or the expected route when a CV signal is suspected, is a long-term controlled outcome study with at least 18 to 24 months of follow-up[174](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=174) .
- **Timing.** An integrated adjudicated MACE analysis is required at submission. A fully powered CV assessment should be submitted before authorization when the mechanism raises an intrinsic concern or a concern emerges during development[175](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=175) .
- **No numerical CV margin.** Revision 1 sets no 1.8 or 1.3 CV margin. Its 0.3% noninferiority margin applies to HbA1c efficacy[177](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=177) .


Revision 2 (CPMP/EWP/1080/00 Rev.2, 2024) points to the separate CHMP reflection paper for CV safety requirements[801](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=801)[803](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=803) .


#### CHMP reflection paper on CV safety


The CHMP reflection paper EMA/CHMP/50549/2015 makes these points:


- **Preferred endpoint.** MACE (CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke) is the preferred endpoint for both pooled analyses and dedicated CVOTs. A broader MACE-plus composite is acceptable only if justified in advance as more sensitive to harm, and each component must be reported[876](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=876) .
- **Adjudication.** An independent committee should adjudicate all major predefined events[264](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=264) .
- **Sensitivity of the data.** Applicants must justify that exposure and follow-up are sufficient. A claim of similar or lower risk should not simply reflect an inability to detect a difference[878](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=878) .
- **Margin.** The general planning assumption is an upper 95% CI bound below 1.8 when the estimated HR is about 1. The paper calls this a reasonable basis at initial licensing, not a universal noninferiority margin, and notes that narrower targets may be appropriate[879](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=879) .


#### Weight management guideline


The CHMP *Guideline on clinical evaluation of medicinal products used in weight management* (EMA/CHMP/311805/2014) expects CV safety to be adequately characterized at MAA. It singles out new mechanisms and drug classes with unestablished or questioned CV safety, and it defers to the reflection paper for quantification[262](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=262) . The final text does not itself mandate a MACE outcome study[252](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=252) .

### How the agencies used CVOT results


#### FDA: standalone risk-reduction indications


FDA has been willing to convert a superior CVOT into a separate indication, usually restricted to the population with the strongest evidence.


- **LEADER (Victoza).** Reviewers accepted a single trial as substantial evidence. They found it large, well conducted, statistically robust and clinically meaningful, with all three MACE components trending favorably[813](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=813)[814](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=814)[815](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=815) . The resulting indication was narrower than the sponsor proposed: adults with type 2 diabetes and *established* CV disease rather than "high CV risk"[818](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=818)[819](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=819) .
- **Jardiance.** FDA framed the benefit around CV death. The review did not consider the single trial enough to conclude a general reduction in macrovascular events[711](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=711)[712](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=712) .
- **SELECT (Wegovy).** FDA's statistical review found no major issues: components were consistent and missing data minimal (3%). CV death, the key secondary endpoint, did not reach superiority, so lower-ranked secondaries could not be called significant[953](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=953) . The approved indication is MACE risk reduction in adults with established CV disease and obesity or overweight[952](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=952) .


Noninferior results go into the label as safety statements, not efficacy claims. Examples are the SAVOR, EXAMINE, CARMELINA, DEVOTE and EXSCEL labeling[284](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=284)[602](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=602)[44](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=44)[653](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=653)[570](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=570) .


#### EMA: section 5.1 with a broadened section 4.1


CHMP followed a consistent pattern:


- **Section 5.1.** CVOT results go into section 5.1.
- **Section 4.1.** The indication changes from "improvement of glycaemic control" to "treatment of" type 2 diabetes, with a cross-reference to section 5.1. CHMP adopted this approach for Victoza, Trulicity and Forxiga[341](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=341)[99](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=99)[678](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=678) .
- **Separate indications declined.** CHMP turned down separate section 4.1 CV indications for Jardiance (CV death), Mounjaro (MACE reduction) and Wegovy (CV prevention). Its reasoning was that the studied populations were already covered by the existing indication[66](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=66)[203](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=203)[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=27) .
- **Steglatro exception.** For Steglatro, CHMP allowed the broadened 4.1 wording even without MACE superiority. It noted that this wording had previously been reserved for products with demonstrated superiority, and justified it on mechanism and class evidence[496](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=496) .


### Methodological issues reviewers raised


- **Post hoc superiority.** CHMP recorded that SUSTAIN 6 was a 1.8-margin safety trial with no prespecified 1.3-then-superiority sequence. Its nominal superiority p value came from an unpenalized post hoc test[618](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=618)[621](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=621) . FDA advisory committee members made a similar point: superiority was not a prespecified test[958](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=958) .
- **What drives the composite.** Regulators looked at which components carried each result:


- EMPA-REG OUTCOME: CV death, with a stroke estimate favoring placebo[64](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=64)[69](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=69)
- SUSTAIN 6: stroke, with similar CV deaths in both arms[624](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=624)
- SELECT: MI, with no overall stroke effect[25](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=25)
- REWIND: no individual component reached significance[102](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=102)


- **Generalizability and subgroups.** CHMP flagged:


- for LEADER, inconsistent benefit in patients without established CV disease and in North America[343](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=343)
- for EMPA-REG OUTCOME, regional inconsistency and a single trial in a high-risk population[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=70)[71](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=71)
- for DECLARE, the small absolute (0.8%) reduction in heart-failure hospitalization[680](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=680)


- **Active-comparator margins.** In SURPASS-CVOT, a placebo-anchored 1.3 margin was not appropriate against an active CV-protective comparator. CHMP accepted a 1.05 margin and considered an indirect placebo comparison via REWIND supportive but not definitive[200](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=200)[206](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=206) .
- **Interim data integrity.** For Contrave, FDA's statistical reviewer recommended keeping the interim LIGHT findings out of labeling. Because of trial-integrity concerns, FDA concluded that LIGHT could not satisfy the postmarketing requirement to exclude 1.4[245](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=245)[246](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=246) . CHMP described the interim data as short- to intermediate-term reassurance only, and some members dissented[516](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=516)[524](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=524) .
- **Heart failure as a separate safety signal.** SAVOR showed a MACE-neutral result alongside more heart-failure hospitalizations. This led to an FDA heart-failure warning and a CHMP caution[289](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=289)[215](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=215) .


### Implications for development programs


- Make adjudicated 3-point MACE the default primary safety endpoint for both agencies. Justify any MACE-plus or ischemic-stroke variant prospectively[876](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=876)[172](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=172) .
- For type 2 diabetes, FDA's current draft position relies on safety-database size and composition rather than a fixed margin[921](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=921)[922](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=922) . EMA defers to the reflection paper's 1.8 planning assumption and case-by-case justification[879](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=879) .
- To support a CV benefit claim, prespecify superiority testing after noninferiority. FDA will grant a standalone indication on one robust trial[813](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=813) . In the EU, expect the result to sit in section 5.1 with a broadened section 4.1 rather than a new CV-prevention indication[341](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=341)[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=27) .
- For obesity drugs, neither agency's guidance sets a numerical MACE margin. A CVOT becomes necessary when a mechanism-based or emergent CV signal exists[750](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=750)[262](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=262) , and the LIGHT precedent shows how interim-analysis integrity affects approval[246](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cardiovascular-outcomes-trials-for-diabetes?showSourceNumber=246) .
